title: Find where a PDLP run converged

blocks.text: A team runs a very large transport LP with PDLP and wants to know, from the log alone, how many iterations a tighter or looser tolerance would have needed, without solving again. PDLP's log reports its progress as a table: each row starts with the iteration number, and the block between the first and second `|` holds three relative measures, `rel_prim_res`, `rel_dual_res` and `rel_gap`.

items: `table_rows(log)` returns every progress row as a tuple `(iteration, rel_prim_res, rel_dual_res, rel_gap)`, in log order. A progress row is a line whose text before the first `|` starts with a whole number; the header row (` iter# ...`) and every other line are skipped. The final-stats row at the end of a log is a progress row too.

`converged_at(log, tol)` returns the iteration of the first progress row where all three measures are within `tol`: $`\text{rel\_prim\_res} \le tol`$, $`\text{rel\_dual\_res} \le tol`$ and $`|\text{rel\_gap}| \le tol`$. The gap is signed, and it is its size that has to be small. If no row gets there, return `None`.

"""Run executes this file. Change the calls and see what prints. Submit grades."""
import logging

# Turn the logger up, so the `log.debug` lines of your code show under the printed lines.
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG, format="%(levelname)s %(message)s")

from converged import converged_at, table_rows

head = " iter# kkt_pass   time | rel_prim_res rel_dual_res      rel_gap |   prim_resid   dual_resid      obj_gap"


def row(iteration, prim, dual, gap):
    return (f"{iteration:6d} {iteration + 1:8.1f}    0.0 | {prim:12.5e} {dual:12.5e} {gap:12.5e} "
            f"|      1.00000      2.00000      3.00000")


log = ["Solving with PDLP", head,
       row(0, 5.0e-2, 0.7, 0.1), row(40, 2.0e-4, 9.0e-5, -3.0e-4), row(80, 4.0e-7, 6.0e-7, 2.0e-7)]
print("rows read:", table_rows(log))
print("converged at tol 1e-3:", converged_at(log, 1e-3))
print("converged at tol 1e-6:", converged_at(log, 1e-6))
print("converged at tol 1e-9:", converged_at(log, 1e-9))

            "     0      0.0    0.0 |  1.00000e-01     0.500000      0.00000 |      3.00000",

cases.says: every progress row is read as iteration and three relative measures, and the header is not
the first row where all three measures are within the tolerance is the answer
a gap of -0.4 is far from converged, since its size is what counts
a row with a large dual residual is not converged, though the other two are small
a log whose rows never get within the tolerance gives None, not its last iteration

origin.section: GLOP and PDLP Logs Carry the Same Facts in Other Words

concepts: PDLP stops at the first check where relative primal residual, dual residual and gap size are all within its tolerance
